title: Failed global hugetlb reservation remains charged to the subpool

classification.cwe_mapping_note: CWE-401 reflects current NVD enrichment; the remaining entries are evaluator classifications. The linked Linux CVE announcement does not assign an official CWE.

finding.incomplete_rollback: When the incremental global reservation fails, the error path returns only the pages covered by the subpool minimum and leaves the failed global portion charged in used_pages.
finding.control_flow: A three-page request raises used_pages from zero to three, one page requires the exhausted global pool, and the failure path rolls back only the other two pages, leaving used_pages at one despite allocating nothing.
finding.impact: Each failed request leaks the global-needed amount into used_pages. Repetition can make the subpool reach its maximum and reject future allocations even though no caller holds those hugepages.
finding.security_property: A failed reservation must be atomic with respect to accounting: allocated_pages must be zero and used_after must equal used_before after all subpool and global charges are rolled back.
finding.expected_fix: On global reservation failure, uncharge global_needed_pages from the subpool used counter in addition to returning the pages covered by the subpool minimum, so rollback_pages equals requested_pages.
finding.model_boundary: The request uses one bounded 4 KiB MiniMM note and transient uint32_t counters capped at 1,000,000. It never mounts hugetlbfs, allocates host hugepages, changes host reservations, or reads or writes the note contents.
